Fixed via a new `kind="ping"` row (already reserved in `LLM_INVOCATION_KINDS`, previously unused) landed once terminal — round 1 review consolidated a duplicate-write draft into a single insert and removed a pointless non-durable `flush()`; round 2 (8 more agents) found two real bugs in THAT refactor: `LLMConfigInvalidError` (a pure config-shape defect, zero network attempt) was being recorded as a completed call, and the round-trip's narrow except let any OTHER exception propagate uncaught — meaning a real, billed call could leave zero trace, the exact gap this issue exists to close. Both fixed; a catch-all now matches `execute_invocation`'s own posture. Plus `_scrub_nul` on the stored error (the #1273 NUL-byte class) and two stale sibling compliance texts corrected. 7 regression tests, all mutation-verified | intelligence |
| ✅ | [#1781](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1781) `execute_invocation` discarded `DataQError.detail`; `llm_rca.py`'s own rejection path had no reason at all — [PR #1786](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1786) merged: `DataQError.__init__` already carries a structured `detail`, but `execute_invocation`'s failure branch discarded it unconditionally and `response` was never set on a failed invocation. Now persisted (scrubbed) alongside `error`; `llm_checksuggest.py`'s all-rejected raise and `llm_rca.py`'s new `_valid_hypothesis` (previously bare `None` on rejection, zero reason captured — worse than checksuggest's own pre-#1780 state) both use it. A 5-agent review pass then found and fixed: no size cap on the persisted `response` (unlike `error`'s `[:1024]` — added `_DETAIL_MAX_CHARS`, oversized detail becomes `{"truncated": True}`); the structured `detail` had no truncation signal of its own (added a `truncated` bool to both payloads); RCA's own message had no total-clause cap unlike checksuggest's (latent today, added anyway); `llm_sqlgen.py` dropped its own validator's `detail` when re-raising (forwarded, closing the 3rd `KIND_VALIDATORS` registrant's inconsistency); RCA's route docstring left stale relative to checksuggest's. Filed [#1787](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1787) (a related but separate pre-existing gap in `check_service.validate_monitor_check`, human-authored-check REST path). 12 regression tests total, all mutation-verified | intelligence |
| ✅ | [#1777](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1777) `llm_invoke` shared the default Celery queue with `run_suite`, false-killable by the pending reaper behind a long `run_suite` backlog — [PR #1789](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1789) merged: `task_routes={LLM_INVOKE_TASK_NAME: {"queue": "llm"}}`, worker command updated to `-Q celery,llm` in all **four** deploy targets (three known + `docker-compose.ghcr.yml`, found by a broader search). 5-agent review found: the task name was independently hardcoded in three places (plus a test) — consolidated into one `LLM_INVOKE_TASK_NAME` constant; two comments this fix itself made stale (a threshold-rationale note, the persisted `_PENDING_REAP_REASON` string); the new comment's own "no longer starves" claim overclaimed (queue separation prevents FIFO fetch-blocking, not execution-slot contention — filed [#1790](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1790), no deploy config sets `--concurrency` despite `perf-baseline.md` claiming 4); and the deploy-ordering hazard (routine image-only rolls would silently orphan `llm_invoke` until Terraform is reapplied) live-confirmed and elevated into an explicit pre-deploy checklist item. 2 regression tests, mutation-verified | intelligence |
| ✅ | [#1772](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1772) P1/security: RCA-narrative evidence carried an unmasked `observed_value`, reaching `get_incident` (REST/MCP), the RCA LLM prompt, AND outbound alert delivery, not just the RCA path the issue named — [PR #1791](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1791) merged: `Incident.evidence` is a stored JSONB snapshot computed ONCE at incident-open/attach time and never recomputed, so all three readers inherited the exposure from one root — `incident_evidence.py::_failing_result_layer`, now routing `observed_value` through `run_service.redact_observed_value` (the same G3 column-policy/warehouse-tag floor every other results surface applies) before the snapshot is ever stored. `expected_value` stays unmasked by design (a check-authored threshold, not warehouse data). Four review passes (efficiency, conventions/docs-honesty, correctness, `mcp-honesty-reviewer`) then found the build-time fix alone does nothing for incidents that already existed — added `incident_service.redact_stale_evidence`, an idempotent one-time backfill (`backend/scripts/redact_stale_incident_evidence.py`), plus a required post-deploy step in `deploy/README.md`. Corrected six now-stale "not yet masked" references across `admin.py`, `llm_rca.py`, and three published compliance docs. Filed [#1792](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1792) (N+1 `historical_check_context` query per failing result, bounded but real) and [#1793](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1793) (a pre-existing, higher-severity fail-open asymmetry in `redact_observed_value` for scalar values when `tested_column` can't be resolved — shared by every results surface, not introduced here, newly exercised by this PR's new caller) rather than expand an already-large security PR further. 5 new regression tests, all mutation-verified | intelligence |

=== #1392 ===
harness: verify the demo environment is actually disposable (tofu destroy never run)
---
Carried over from the (now-retired) local `HARNESS_TODO.md` §1, where it sat unchecked since the harness was first stood up.

## The gap

The harness stack is described as a disposable demo environment, but **`destroy` has never been run against it**. That makes "disposable" an assumption rather than a verified property — and teardown is exactly the operation that tends to fail the first time it is attempted (dependency ordering, resources created outside state, providers that cannot authenticate against an already-dead host).

This matters for two things that depend on it:
- **Gap G-i** — the pre-marketplace teardown (strip Flows A/B/C, harness connections, demo users) before any customer-facing artifact.
- Cost wind-down, where the fallback if `destroy` misbehaves is hand-deleting resources and hoping nothing is missed.

## Important: this must NOT be run casually

A blanket harness `apply` arms both ADF triggers and drifts the warehouse; a blanket **`destroy` is worse** — it would take out the live infra behind the Azure demo flows. So this issue is deliberately *not* "run `tofu destroy`".

Do it one of these ways:
1. **Rehearsal (safe, do this first):** `tofu plan -destroy` and read the full resource list. Confirm it is complete and correctly ordered, and identify anything created outside state.
2. **Scoped proof:** `-target` a single leaf resource that is cheap to recreate, destroy it, re-apply, verify it comes back.
3. **Full destroy:** only at actual wind-down, when the environment is genuinely finished with.

## Known complications already recorded

- The UC catalog was **created in the UI and imported** into state — it will be destroyed by OpenTofu, which is the intent but is worth confirming in the plan.
- The **hidden westus2 Postgres name reservation is external to state** and will survive a destroy.
- The harness Postgres is **shared with the DataQ app stack** (1-of-each free/trial cap) — a destroy must not take the app database with it. Verify this explicitly in the plan output.

Related: #588 (retiring the Snowflake leg specifically at subscription lapse) covers one leg gracefully; this covers whether the whole stack tears down at all.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tofu plan -destroy` reviewed in full; the resource list is complete and the ordering is sound
- [ ] Confirmed the plan does **not** include the shared Postgres server or the DataQ app stack
- [ ] Out-of-state survivors (the westus2 name reservation, any others found) documented in the harness README
- [ ] Either a scoped destroy+re-apply proof, or a full destroy at wind-down, recorded in `docs/ops-log.md` with UTC timestamps




=== #1257 ===
harness: narrow DATAQ_LOADER's account-wide MANAGE GRANTS to just the dbt on-run-end hook's need
---
Follow-up noted in `docs/ops-log.md` ("Finding 2026-07-27 — #1032's credential swap left DATAQ_LOADER short two grants") when closing #1030/#1032, never filed as its own tracked item.

## What

`DATAQ_LOADER` currently holds `GRANT MANAGE GRANTS ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE DATAQ_LOADER` (granted 2026-07-27 ~06:55), needed only so the dbt `on-run-end` hook can `GRANT SELECT/USAGE` on the two dbt-created schemas (`ANALYTICS_STG`, `ANALYTICS`) to `DATAQ_READER`. `MANAGE GRANTS` is account-wide — far broader than the two-schema need.

## Suggested direction

Per the ops-log's own note, either:
- Grant schema-scoped ownership instead: `GRANT OWNERSHIP ON SCHEMA DATAQ_DB.ANALYTICS_STG TO ROLE DATAQ_LOADER COPY CURRENT GRANTS` (+ `ANALYTICS`), which was the original #1030 suggestion, narrower than account-wide `MANAGE GRANTS`.
- Or pre-create FUTURE grants to `DATAQ_READER` on those two schemas and delete the `on-run-end` hook entirely, removing the need for `MANAGE GRANTS` altogether.

## Scope

Harness-only (Snowsight + `~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/dbt/` on-run-end hook config), not app code. Low urgency — this is privilege-scoping hygiene on a demo-scoped harness account, not a live security exposure in the DataQ product itself.

Refs #1030, #1032, #609.



=== #1775 ===
mcp: reusable notification channels (#1514/#1662/#1663) have no MCP tool coverage at all
---
## Summary
Reusable notification channels (Teams/Slack/email/generic-webhook, #1514/#1662/#1663) have full REST CRUD but zero MCP tools. Found while extending `get_notification_config` to recognize a suite-linked channel as a third alert-configuration source (\`*_source: \"channel\"\`) — that new value has no companion tool an LLM client could call to find out *which* channel it is, or what type.

## Impact
An LLM client asking "who gets told when orders fails?" via `get_notification_config` can now correctly see `email_recipients_source: "channel"` (a linked reusable channel is why email delivers) but has no way to identify or inspect that channel — no `list_channels`, no `get_channel`, no `list_channels_for_suite` equivalent exists on the MCP surface.

## Fix
Add read-only MCP tools mirroring the REST read surface: something like `list_notification_channels` (workspace-wide) and `list_suite_channels` (suite-scoped), following the same "presence not value" discipline already established for webhook/HMAC secrets in this codebase (never resolve or return a credential — `has_webhook`, `has_hmac_secret`, `has_auth_header` style booleans only). Mutation tools (create/update/delete/link/unlink) are a separate, later decision — the #1514/#1662/#1663 work already establishes admin-gating and credential-redaction conventions to follow if/when that's added.

Found during PR #1774 (get_notification_config's SMTP-gate fix) review.



=== #1761 ===

## Problem

#1514 (reusable notification channels — define a Teams/Slack/email channel once, reference it from many suites) shipped backend-only: schema (`notification_channels` + `suite_notification_channels`), `channel_service.py` (Admin-gated CRUD, suite-scoped link/unlink), REST API (`/notification-channels`, `/suites/{id}/notification-channels`), alerting fan-out (Teams/Slack/email publishers now deliver to every linked channel, deduped against the legacy per-suite/workspace destination, with per-destination failure isolation), and the secret-sweep ownership registry. @dataclass(frozen=True)
class OutcomePhase:
    """One unit of execution: ``(check index, outcome)`` pairs plus whether the
    phase's rows may be committed as soon as built (#318) — see
    `_run_outcome_phases` for the publishability rule.
    """

    resolved: list[tuple[int, CheckOutcome]]
    publishable: bool


def _run_outcome_phases(
    runner: CheckRunner,
    *,
    table: str,
    schema: str | None,
    checks: list[Check],
    index_columns: list[str] | None = None,
    comparison_executor: Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome] | None = None,
    stateful_monitor_executor: Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome] | None = None,
) -> Iterator[OutcomePhase]:
    """Run a suite's checks, dispatched by `check.kind` (ADR 0012), yielding each
    unit of execution as it resolves.
    """

    # Engine partition first (ADR 0036): native checks route via `run_native_check` when
    # advertised, else a per-check `error` — never a silent skip or a sibling-killing raise.
    def _engine(c: Check) -> str:
        return c.engine or GX_ENGINE

    advertised = frozenset(getattr(runner, "supported_native_engines", frozenset()))
    native_run = getattr(runner, "run_native_check", None)
    for i, c in enumerate(checks):
        engine = _engine(c)
        if engine == GX_ENGINE:
            continue
        if engine in advertised and callable(native_run):
            outcome = cast(
                CheckOutcome,
                native_run(
                    kind=c.kind,
                    expectation_type=c.expectation_type,
                    config=dict(c.config),
                    table=table,
                    schema=schema,
                ),
            )
        else:
            outcome = _executor_outcome(
                None,
                c,
                missing=(
                    f"engine '{engine}' is not available on this "
                    "connection — the check was authored for a "
                    "platform-native engine this deployment cannot run "
                    "(ADR 0036); re-check the connection's engine "
                    "capabilities or re-point the check to 'gx'"
                ),
            )
        yield OutcomePhase(resolved=[(i, outcome)], publishable=True)
    checks_gx = [(i, c) for i, c in enumerate(checks) if _engine(c) == GX_ENGINE]
    expectation_idx = [i for i, c in checks_gx if c.kind == _EXPECTATION_KIND]
    monitor_idx = [i for i, c in checks_gx if c.kind in SCALAR_MONITOR_KINDS]
    stateful_idx = [i for i, c in checks_gx if c.kind in STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS]
    comparison_idx = [i for i, c in checks_gx if c.kind == COMPARISON_KIND]
    handled = {_EXPECTATION_KIND, *MONITOR_KINDS, COMPARISON_KIND}
    # GX partition only: native-engine checks were already resolved above.
    unsupported = sorted({c.kind for _, c in checks_gx if c.kind not in handled})
    if unsupported:
        raise NotImplementedError(f"no run path for check kind(s) {', '.join(unsupported)}")

            name=f"suite-{table}",
            # index_columns deliberately NOT folded: live-verified 2026-08-28 that GX's
            # unexpected_index_column_names path accepts the authored (upper) casing and keys
            # the locators by it — folding would lowercase the locator keys users see.
            index_columns=index_columns,
        )

    def run_native_check(
        self,
        *,
        kind: str,
        expectation_type: str,
        config: dict[str, Any],
        table: str,
        schema: str | None,
    ) -> CheckOutcome:
        """Evaluate ONE dmf-engine check via ad-hoc system-DMF SQL (ADR 0036)."""
        from sqlalchemy import text

        with self._engine.get().connect() as conn:
            return evaluate_dmf_check(
                lambda statement: conn.execute(text(statement)).scalar(),
                kind=kind,
                expectation_type=expectation_type,
                config=config,
                table=table,
                schema=schema or self._config.schema_,
            )

    def run_monitors(
        self, *, table: str, schema: str | None, monitors: list[MonitorSpec]
    ) -> list[CheckOutcome]:
        """Evaluate freshness/volume monitors via scalar SQL aggregates (no GX)."""
        return run_monitors_over_engine(
            self._engine.get(),
            table=table,
            schema=schema or self._config.schema_,
            catalog=None,
            monitors=monitors,
        )

def validate_engine(engine: str, *, connection_type: str) -> None:
    """Reject an engine the suite's connection doesn't offer (422, ADR 0036 §5)."""
    if engine not in CHECK_ENGINES:
        raise CheckConfigInvalidError(
            f"check engine {engine!r} is not recognised",
            detail={"engine": engine, "known": sorted(CHECK_ENGINES)},
        )
    offered = engines_for(connection_type)
    if engine not in offered:
        raise CheckConfigInvalidError(
            f"engine {engine!r} is not offered by this suite's connection "
            f"(type {connection_type!r}) — ADR 0036 anchors native engines to "
            "the connection that can run them",
            detail={
                "engine": engine,
                "connection_type": connection_type,
                "offered": sorted(offered),
            },
        )


def validate_engine_compatibility(
    engine: str,
    *,
    kind: str,
    expectation_type: str,
    config: dict[str, Any],
    warn_threshold: Decimal | None,
    fail_threshold: Decimal | None,
    critical_threshold: Decimal | None,
) -> None:
    """The engine's supported matrix (ADR 0036 §4) — 422 for a kind/type/config
    the engine cannot evaluate. Shared by create, update, restore and suite
    import (the one-gate-per-rule discipline).
    """
    if engine != DMF_ENGINE:
        return
    if kind not in DMF_KINDS:
        raise CheckConfigInvalidError(
            f"the dmf engine cannot evaluate kind {kind!r} — it evaluates "
            "freshness and the dmf:* column metrics",
            detail={"engine": engine, "kind": kind, "supported_kinds": sorted(DMF_KINDS)},
        )
    if kind != "expectation":
        return  # freshness/volume config is the monitor validators' job
    if expectation_type not in DMF_EXPECTATION_TYPES:
        raise CheckConfigInvalidError(
            f"expectation_type {expectation_type!r} is not a dmf metric",
            detail={"engine": engine, "supported_types": sorted(DMF_EXPECTATION_TYPES)},
        )

    if unknown_keys:
        raise CheckConfigInvalidError(
            f"a dmf column metric's config is exactly {{'column': …}}; unknown keys: "

def _dry_run_native(
    connection: Connection,
    *,
    engine: str,
    kind: str,
    expectation_type: str,
    config: dict[str, Any],
    warn_threshold: Decimal | None,
    fail_threshold: Decimal | None,
    critical_threshold: Decimal | None,
    target: dict[str, Any] | None,
    secret_store: SecretStore,
) -> DryRunOutcome:
    """Preview a platform-native (ADR 0036) check via the connection's own
    ``run_native_check`` — the same partition `run_service._run_outcome_phases`
    uses for a persisted run, so a preview never routes a dmf/dqx check through
    the GX runner (#1530).
    """
    resolved = run_target.resolve_target(connection.type, target)
    try:
        runner = build_check_runner(
            conn_type=connection.type,
            config=connection.config,
            secret_ref=connection.secret_ref,
            secret_store=secret_store,
            catalog=resolved.catalog,
            sampling=resolved.sampling,
        )
    except UnsupportedConnectionTypeError as exc:
        raise DryRunUnsupportedError(
            f"dry-run is not supported for {connection.type!r} connections",
            detail={"type": connection.type},
        ) from exc
    except Exception as exc:
        log.warning(
            "dry_run_failed", connection_type=connection.type, error_type=type(exc).__name__
        )
        raise DryRunFailedError(
            "dry run could not connect to the datasource",
            detail={"reason": safe_failure_reason(exc)},
        ) from exc

    with owned_runner(runner):
        native_run = getattr(runner, "run_native_check", None)
        advertised = frozenset(getattr(runner, "supported_native_engines", frozenset()))
        if engine not in advertised or not callable(native_run):
            raise DryRunUnsupportedError(
                f"engine {engine!r} is not available on this connection — the connection "
                "cannot run this platform-native engine (ADR 0036)",
                detail={"engine": engine, "connection_type": connection.type},
            )
        try:
            table = run_target.materialize_path(
                connection.type,
                connection.config,
                resolved,
                secret_ref=connection.secret_ref,
                secret_store=secret_store,
            )
        except BatchNotFoundError as exc:
            raise DryRunNoDataError(
                "no file has landed for the suite's batch target yet — dry-run needs live data",
                detail={"connection_type": connection.type},
            ) from exc
        except DataQError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            log.warning(
                "dry_run_failed", connection_type=connection.type, error_type=type(exc).__name__
            )
            raise DryRunFailedError(
                "dry run could not list the datasource store",
                detail={"reason": safe_failure_reason(exc)},
            ) from exc

        try:
            check_outcome = native_run(
                kind=kind,
                expectation_type=expectation_type,
                config=dict(config),
                table=table,
                schema=resolved.schema,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            log.warning(
                "dry_run_failed", connection_type=connection.type, error_type=type(exc).__name__
            )
            raise DryRunFailedError(
                "dry run could not execute against the datasource",
                detail={"table": table, "reason": safe_failure_reason(exc)},
            ) from exc

        status, metric = resolve_status(
            check_outcome,
            warn_threshold=warn_threshold,
            fail_threshold=fail_threshold,
            critical_threshold=critical_threshold,
        )
        if check_outcome.errored:
            error_message = strip_statement_echo(check_outcome.error_message)
            observed = {"error": error_message} if error_message else None
        else:
            observed = sanitize_json(check_outcome.observed_value)
        return DryRunOutcome(
            status=status,
            metric_value=metric,
            observed_value=observed,
            expected_value=sanitize_json(check_outcome.expected_value),
        )

link/unlink on the suite's own view/edit ladder. Mirrors the `/connections`
split: reads are open to any authenticated user (a suite editor picks a channel
from a list), mutations are `AdminUser`-only (a webhook URL is a credential).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from typing import Annotated, Any, Literal

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, status
from pydantic import Field
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.api.v1._base import ApiModel, ApiRequestModel
from backend.app.core.auth import AdminUser, get_current_user
from backend.app.core.roles import is_workspace_admin

from backend.app.services import channel_service as svc
from backend.app.services.suite_authz import require_permission

router = APIRouter(tags=["notification-channels"])


class ChannelRead(ApiModel):
    """A channel's shape as any authenticated caller may see it. The Teams/Slack
    webhook and the generic webhook's HMAC signing key are credentials and
    never returned, only whether one is set — `webhook_url` is the exception:
    for a generic webhook it is the destination, not the credential (the HMAC
    signature is), so it is safe to echo back for admin visibility.

    `payload_template` is a partial exception: it isn't itself a SecretStore-
    backed credential column, but an admin authoring one (e.g. a PagerDuty
    Events-API body) commonly has nowhere else to put that receiver's static
    routing/integration key than as a literal in the template JSON — which
    functions as a credential even though the field's storage doesn't treat
    it as one (#1663 review). It's therefore only ever included for an
    Admin caller; every other authenticated user gets `has_payload_template`
    instead, the same presence-only shape already used for genuine secrets.
    """

    id: uuid.UUID
    name: str
    type: str
    has_webhook: bool
    email_recipients: str | None
    webhook_url: str | None = None
    has_hmac_secret: bool = False
    #: Populated ONLY by create/rotate, in the response of that one call — the
    #: plaintext HMAC signing key, shown exactly once. Never set by a read.
    hmac_secret: str | None = None
    #: Admin-only — see the class docstring. `None` for a non-admin caller
    #: regardless of whether a template is actually set; use
    #: `has_payload_template` to tell "unset" from "set but not shown".
    payload_template: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    has_payload_template: bool = False
    auth_header_name: str | None = None

auth_header_name: str | None = None
    has_auth_header: bool = False

    @classmethod
    def from_model(
        cls,
        channel: NotificationChannel,
        *,
        hmac_secret: str | None = None,
        include_payload_template: bool = True,
    ) -> ChannelRead:
        return cls(
            id=channel.id,
            name=channel.name,
            type=channel.type,
            has_webhook=channel.webhook_secret_ref is not None,
            email_recipients=channel.email_recipients,
            webhook_url=channel.webhook_url,
            has_hmac_secret=channel.hmac_secret_ref is not None,
            hmac_secret=hmac_secret,
            payload_template=channel.payload_template if include_payload_template else None,
            has_payload_template=channel.payload_template is not None,
            auth_header_name=channel.auth_header_name,
            has_auth_header=channel.auth_header_secret_ref is not None,
        )


class ChannelCreate(ApiRequestModel):
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)
    type: Literal["teams", "slack", "email", "webhook"]
    webhook: str | None = Field(default=None, description="Teams/Slack webhook URL; write-only")
    email_recipients: str | None = Field(default=None, description="Comma-separated addresses")
    webhook_url: str | None = Field(

    )
    payload_template: dict[str, Any] | None = Field(

            "(PagerDuty/Opsgenie/ServiceNow/Jira). {{field.path}} placeholders "

    )
    auth_header_name: str | None = Field(

class ChannelUpdate(ApiRequestModel):

        default=None, description="Set the auth header name; empty string clears it"
    )
    auth_header_value: str | None = None


@router.get("/notification-channels", response_model=list[ChannelRead], summary="List channels")

Implement GitHub issue #1775 in the DataQ repo. Work on a NEW branch off main named `feat/issue-1775-mcp-channel-read-tools`, commit, push, and open a PR titled "mcp: read-only tools for reusable notification channels" targeting main, with milestone "v1.2 Week 5 — native engines (DMF) + notification channels". End the commit message with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" and the PR body with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)".

## Background
Reusable notification channels (#1514/#1662/#1663 — Teams/Slack/email/generic-webhook, admin-defined, linked per-suite) shipped full REST CRUD (`backend/app/api/v1/notification_channels.py`) but have ZERO MCP tool coverage. `get_notification_config` (MCP, `backend/app/mcp/server.py` around line 1435) can now report `*_source: "channel"` when a suite's alert config comes from a linked reusable channel, but there's no MCP tool to identify or inspect that channel.

## What to build
Two new read-only MCP tools in `backend/app/mcp/server.py`, mirroring the REST read surface (`channel_service.list_channels` / `list_channels_for_suite`, and the `ChannelRead` shape in `backend/app/api/v1/notification_channels.py`):

1. `list_notification_channels()` — workspace-wide list of all channels. No suite scoping needed (channels are a workspace resource visible to any authenticated user per REST — `list_channels` in `notification_channels.py` has no suite-authz check). This puts it in the "no per-resource gate" group in `backend/tests/support/mcp_gates.py` (alongside `list_connections`, `list_suites`) — gate value `"read"`.

2. `list_suite_channels(suite_id)` — channels linked to one suite (`channel_service.list_channels_for_suite`). Gated on the suite like other suite-scoped reads (`suite:view` in `mcp_gates.py`, alongside `list_checks`/`get_notification_config`).

## Critical constraint: presence, not value
This codebase has an established, load-bearing discipline for credentials on this exact table: **never resolve or return a credential — only a presence boolean.** Read `ChannelRead.from_model` in `backend/app/api/v1/notification_channels.py` closely — it returns `has_webhook`, `has_hmac_secret`, `has_payload_template` (admin-only, else `has_payload_template` boolean), `has_auth_header`, and only echoes `webhook_url` itself (destination, not the credential — the HMAC signature is what secures it) and `payload_template` (admin-only, see its docstring on WHY). Your MCP tool payloads must follow the exact same shape: never a webhook secret, never an HMAC secret, never `auth_header_value`. `payload_template` should probably follow the same admin-gating REST does (check `is_workspace_admin` — `backend/app/core/roles.py`) if you include it at all; simplest safe choice is to omit `payload_template` entirely from the MCP payload and just expose `has_payload_template`, unless you find a clean way to reuse `ChannelRead`'s own admin gating logic.

## LLM-honesty requirements (this file has a documented failure history — read carefully)
This MCP surface (`backend/app/mcp/server.py`) has produced 50+ real honesty defects in this codebase's history: partial-as-final, unknown-as-zero, a null meaning two things, docstrings that are false (not just thin), and — most relevant here — **a new tool falsifying a sibling tool's docstring that named its absence as the workaround**. Specifically:
- `get_notification_config`'s docstring currently explains `*_source: "channel"` in some way that either doesn't mention a way to inspect it, or points elsewhere — READ that docstring first and update it to point at `list_suite_channels`/`list_notification_channels` now that they exist, if it needs it.
- Every tool docstring must state what the tool does NOT show (the credential values) plainly, not just imply it via field naming.
- Field naming must be self-explanatory to a model with no other context: `has_webhook`, `has_hmac_secret`, `type`, etc.

## Process
1. Read `backend/app/services/channel_service.py` (`list_channels`, `list_channels_for_suite`) and `backend/app/api/v1/notification_channels.py` (`ChannelRead`) fully before writing anything.
2. Follow the existing MCP tool patterns in `server.py` closely (e.g. `list_connections`, `list_checks` for docstring style, `_ctx()`/`_service_errors()` usage, `require_permission` for the suite-scoped tool).
3. Add both tools' gates to `backend/tests/support/mcp_gates.py`'s `GATES` dict in the correct alphabetical group.
4. Write tests in `backend/tests/mcp/test_mcp_tools.py` following existing conventions — at minimum: both tools return the right shape, no credential value ever appears in the payload (assert on this explicitly, not just check the field name), the suite-scoped tool enforces its gate (view access required), and the RBAC sweep passes.
5. **Before finishing, run the mcp-honesty-reviewer subagent (via the Agent tool, subagent_type "mcp-honesty-reviewer") on your own diff to server.py and address its findings** — this is mandatory for this file per the project's working agreement (a PostToolUse hook enforces it on every server.py edit).
6. Run ruff/black/mypy on changed files, and the full `tests/mcp/` suite (`conda run -n dataq python -m pytest tests/mcp/ -q --no-cov` from `backend/`) to confirm no regressions.
7. Update `get_notification_config`'s docstring if it references the absence of a channel-inspection tool.

Report back: what you built, the mcp-honesty-reviewer's findings and how you addressed them, test results, and the PR URL.

Add `engine` to `list_check_versions`' per-version dict (and its docstring's field enumeration) and consider a per-check `engine` field on `get_run_results`/`get_suite_results` (or a docstring caveat pointing at `get_check`).

Refs #1531, PR #1868
EOF

cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ
gh issue create --title "privacy: zero-sample suppression is indistinguishable from 'nothing to redact' on a single result" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
Found by /code-review on PR #1872 (#1676 zero-sample privacy mode). `ResultRead.redaction` (`api/v1/runs.py`) is documented as "null means 'no sample'". Under `PRIVACY_ZERO_SAMPLE_MODE=true`, every failed check's `sample_failures`/list-shaped `observed_value` is nulled at write time — `redact_sample_failures_with_state(None, ...)` returns `(None, None, [])` because `_RedactionTracker` never records anything when the input is already `None`.

## Impact
A genuinely-failed check with real (would-be) violating rows now reports `sample_failures: null, redaction: null` — the identical shape a passing check, or an aggregate-only expectation type, has always produced. An auditor, the Admin UI, or an LLM reading a single result via REST/MCP has no way to tell "nothing to redact" from "suppressed for privacy" from that result alone. The only place this is visible is the deployment-level `GET /admin/deployment.zero_sample_mode` flag — no per-result field carries it forward.

## Fix (needs a design decision, not just a patch)
Options: (a) a new `redaction: "zero_sample"` state value (extends the existing enum rather than overloading `null`), (b) a boolean flag on the result read model, or (c) accept the deployment-level-only signal as sufficient (an auditor already knows the mode is on) and just document the limitation clearly. Recorded here rather than decided unilaterally, per the "fixed or filed" rule — not fixed in #1872 to avoid scope creep on an already-large fix.

Refs #1676, PR #1872
EOF
)" \
  --label "enhancement" --milestone "v1.2 Week 5 — native engines (DMF) + notification channels"
